NFL Week 1 Preview

These are the things I’m looking at on this week’s slate:

- Bengals vs. Bucs looks like a game with a median outcome around 27-24. I don’t have very much confidence in Zac Taylor, but I’m sure he knows you should try to beat Todd Bowles’ defenses through the air.

- When these teams squared off in 2022, Joe Burrow threw for four scores, while Ja’Marr Chase went for 7-60-1 on a game leading 13 targets. In 2020 when Tyreek Hill went for 13-269-3 on 15 targets against Tampa in the regular season, Bowles took a different approach in the Super Bowl, by playing more two high and sending less heat (which they also didn’t need because KC was down both starting OTs). Hill went for 7-73 in that second bout. Hill is a unique player, but the point I’m trying to make here is if Bowles is going to send less heat and play more two high in a game, giving Chase volume underneath like he did to Hill in the Super Bowl, would make sense.

- If this game ends up going under, good chance this type of dynamic is a factor.

- I have never been a Bucky Irving guy, but I like Bucky Irving in this spot. I also like Emeka Egbuka and to a lesser extent Chris Godwin.

- If the Chicago Bears play reasonably well, they should be able to beat the Carolina Panthers with some distance. The question for me is what kind of macro gameplan does Ben Johnson have against a Panthers defense whose strength is linebacker and perimeter corner, paired with a below average pass rush? Everything is on the table against this opponent, so how aggressive Johnson comes out is of great interest to me, because Chicago could win big in both phases against the Panthers.

- Carolina isn’t built to be a shootout team, so I’d think that Dave Canales will lean into the old school completions plus carries brand of offense for as long as he can, similar to the one they took against Dallas last year. Get Bryce Young some layups early with a run heavy approach, unless they are forced out of it.

- The Falcons may have attempted to play real offense if Tua Tagovailoa was active, which probably would have been a disaster against the Steelers’ defense.

- With Cooper Rush at the controls my expectation is a muddier, more Bijan Robinson-centric game plan with some early quick hitters in an effort to mitigate Pittsburgh’s front. I’d expect a play action shot play mixed in early as well.

- Aaron Rodgers is no longer at the peak of his powers, and he had a few bad games in 2025. But he also had plenty of solid outings, with a few remarkable ones for a quarterback that’s breached 40 years old. If Rodgers plays well here, it’s tough to see Pittsburgh losing this one.

- The Eagles have a vastly superior roster to Washington, with advantages in both trenches.

- This looks like a potential smash spot for Saquon Barkley.

- Apart from Jayden Daniels putting the Commanders on his back and carrying them to victory against a superior roster, it’s difficult to see a path for Washington to win this contest.

- Hosting the Saints is a perfect Opening Day opponent for the Lions offense, as Jared Goff could realistically throw for 300 yards and 4 TDs, or Jahmyr Gibbs could approach 200 total yards against this defense.

- Any of the Lions core skill players could pop off here, but I like Sam Laporta’s matchup more than I usually do.

- I was very impressed with Kellen Moore last year, but there are now 10 games of film on Tyler Shough that opponents have had an offseason to review. If I’m Detroit playing Shough, I make him beat me with perimeter throws, similar to how Bill Belichick gave Tom Brady nothing on in breakers in their first matchup as foes (no, I am not comparing Shough to Brady in any capacity).

- It would not surprise me if the Colts beat Baltimore. Lamar Jackson in a new offense, against an opponent specific DC in Lou Anarumo that’s very familiar with Jackson.

- Shane Steichen’s offense also hung 38 points against Jesse Minter’s Chargers defense in the first half of last year, in one of the better games Daniel Jones has played in his career.

- My favorite aspect of the Jaguars’ non-quarterback roster is their front four, and that group could derail this game against Cleveland’s bottom tier offensive line.

- I treat Florida home games in September as an edge.

- Jacksonville also has coaching continuity and Trevor Lawrence, who ascended to at least fringe top 10 status at the position last season. That’s four real advantages for the Jaguars.

- I like Todd Monken, which is why I feel bad for him that he had to take this job, it reminds me a bit of when Vic Fangio took the Broncos job. Because this Browns team, while it has some good building blocks for the future, is a mess as it stands today. If Cleveland makes this interesting, their still pretty good defense drives that outcome in a rare road spike game for this group, with the expectation that Todd Monken builds at least one scoring drive around explosive rookie KC Concepcion.

- I don’t have any doubt that the Chargers will have a high-performing offense this season with Mike McDaniel calling plays for Justin Herbert. I could however see a monumental fall off for this defense with Jessie Minter in Baltimore.

- This looks like a potential smash spot for Omarion Hampton, though in reality this is a very good matchup for every core component of the Chargers’ offense.

- If the Jacoby Brissett we saw last year is the one we’ll get on Sunday, I don’t think Arizona wins this game, but I could see them keeping up and hanging around.

- Michael Wilson really surprised me last year, good looking physical/ contested catch player. I have no pushback on Arizona extending Wilson for real money. Given that, it’s time for Marvin Harison Jr. to become even 90% of who he was supposed to.

- The Texans pass rush beat the Buffalo Bills last year behind an 8-sack effort. Joe Brady was given a tremendous opportunity this offseason in Buffalo, it would be nice to see him create some margin against a high-end defense.

- Davis Mills was Houston’s quarterback for this contest last season, which again was carried by the Texans defense. If rookie year CJ Stroud is still in there, Houston is a legit Super Bowl contender, bordering on the team no one in the AFC wants to play. If the Stroud of the last two seasons is the actual reality, which I think it is, this matchup with Buffalo will be a good litmus test, because this is a very average defense these days.

- Titans vs. Jets has a 38.5 game total, but this game has some shootout potential as both teams have pretty good wide receiver rooms against back-of-the-pack secondaries. Additionally, Cam Ward and Geno Smith both have some ceiling to their games.  No one can trust either of these teams, at this stage, but if this game approached 60 total points, it would not shock me.

- If De’Von Achane is going to have a day this season, this game in Vegas is one of his best shots.

- A few people I hold in high-regard like Malik Willis here. I’m expecting this game to be close to unwatchable. Hope I’m wrong.

- I was pretty interested in seeing how Klint Kubiak would put defenders in horrendous positions with Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. While that’s off the table here, Michael Mayer is one of the best TE2’s in the league and a player that would start on several teams.

- If Maxx Crosby has a monster game, Vegas should start shopping him again, because as I’ve said for nearly two years now, he’s the one piece this organization has that can help them build the interesting future they are now on track to enjoy.

- Vikings vs. Packers might be the most interesting game on the slate. On the Packers side, this looks like a game Jordan Love needs to carry. While I think we’ve already seen the best days of Love’s Packers from a team success slant, I do think he’s positioned to have his most productive season. But in Minnesota, against Brian Flores, behind a questionable offensive line is a tough Opening Day draw.

- Flores is probably the worst opponent in the league for this, but given that Green Bay has lost their skill position depth this offseason, I really want to see what the target distribution looks like in this offense.

- I can’t wait to see what Kyler Murray looks like with Kevin O’Connell. Peak Murray would be a perennial MVP contender in this environment, especially if he started his career with a value-add play caller like O’Connell.

- Giants vs. Cowboys shouldn’t be the first Sunday night game of the year, and I’m pretty surprised the total is 48.5.

- If the Giants still had Dexter Lawrence, Dallas being down Tyler Smith would be a real problem. Since Lawrence is in Cincinnati, New York doesn’t have the tools to exploit that loss unless it’s with a third and long stunt.

- If New York is going to be a competitive team their edge rush needs to get them off the field on third down, and this secondary needs to take one, if not two leaps forward. Dallas is a very good test on both fronts.

- Jaxson Dart can play when he doesn’t face a stacked pass rush, so this is a good spot for him to have a solid game.

- Chiefs vs. Broncos is an excellent Monday Night Football game. Kansas City is down their starting LT, which is a problem against a team like Denver. Strong chance Andy Reid uses the run and quick passing game to mitigate that disparity early in this matchup.

- I would love for some shades of Reid’s old screen game to show up in this matchup, especially if he doesn’t call the first one for a while.

- The Broncos offense against Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is a really good coaching duel. Denver’s offense has more talent than Kansas City’s defense, but Spagnuolo has gotten the most out of this group for years.

I’ve watched every NFL game for roughly a decade now, which I do for sports speculation purposes.

I run a reality-based program here.

If you want me to keep doing this every week, comment or share this. As long as engagement justifies the time, I’ll keep putting stuff like this out consistently.

Happy 32nd Birthday to the gorgeous, massively talented chart-topping, history-making, award-winning Rapstar, Lyrical Maestro, Composer, Record Producer, Superstar and Cultural & Global Icon, the Legendary One & Only RM who rings in his 32nd on top of the World, currently the most trending artist across all social media platforms! 👏🥳🎂🎉🎈🌟💥1⃣🌎🐐👑💙 
#RM exploded on the music scene as the visionary leader and lead Rapper of #BTS, the Biggest Boy Band in the world who paved the way for many! Kim Namjoon is the brain and backbone of BTS, a rare pop star who can command a stadium, a UN podium, and a museum wing with the same brilliance! He's the key behind BTS becoming a planet-scale phenomenon by writing the words that made millions feel seen, including self-love anthems, and the kind of Korean-to-the-world honesty that made “Speak Yourself” a generation’s rallying cry. He's one of the sharpest Rappers and a huge solo star in his own right, with albums like 'Indigo' and 'Right Place, Wrong Person' making music history! His art collecting is so serious that SFMOMA is staging his own collection! As a cultural diplomat, and ambassador to the National Museum of Korea, RM is the only one who can talk APEC CEOs into taking K-culture seriously! He's the leader who didn’t just front the biggest band on the planet—he gave it a mind! 

RM is the World's most influential Leader, and an inspiration to Millions around the Globe! He has an incredible deep baritone voice, and is one of the World's top Solo Artists, surpassing 3.375 BILLION streams on his solo Spotify profile, the only K-Pop Rapper with Agust D and j hope to reach this milestone! He's the 10th overall Most-Streamed K-Pop Soloist in history and the 4th most followed K-Pop Soloist on Spotify after V, jhope & Jungkook and the 8th Most Followed K-Pop Act with over 19.6 Million followers thanks to his poetic lyricism and genre-blending solo projects like 'Indigo' which have earned him a major following! He ties with PSY & JIMIN for the K-Pop Soloist with the 4th most No. 1s in World Digital Song Sales chart history (5)! In 2015 he released his first solo mixtape, 'RM', followed by his record-breaking 2nd mixtape, 'mono.' in 2018, which broke the record for the Most No. 1s in iTunes history (125)! 'mono.' became the highest-charting album by a K-Soloist in U.S. history, peaking at #26 on the Billboard 200! With 'mono.', RM became the 1st Kpop Soloist to reach #1 on the Billboard Emerging Artist Chart!  With his 2nd studio album, 'Right Place, Wrong Person',  Namjoon made history, becoming the 1st  Kpop Soloist with multiple albums debuting inside the Top 5 of the Billboard 200! RM was also the First Korean Act to hit #1 on the R&B and Hip-Hop Digital Sales Charts! RM is the 3rd most credited Idol by the Korean Music Copyright Association KOMCA, after Bang Chan & Ravi, with 238 songs credited to his name!  

RM began his music career in his teens in the underground Korean hip-hop scene under the name of Runch Randa. He joined Big Hit in 2010, and debuted as part of BTS in June 2013. RM released his 1st solo mixtape, 'RM', in 2015, and his 2nd mixtape, 'Mono.' in 2018 which became the highest-charting album by a Korean solo artist in US history at the time, peaking at No. 26 on the Billboard 200! RM made his official solo debut in 2022 with the release of his hugely successful history-making studio album 'Indigo', which features Erykah Badu and Anderson Paak amongst others. The album reached #3 on the Billboard 200, and was the highest-charting album by a K-Soloist in US chart history at the time!  All songs of 'Indigo' debuted in the Global Spotify Top 100 with 8 tracks simultaneously charting on the World Digital Song Sales chart! 'Indigo' debuted at #1 on the Billboard World Albums Chart and became the longest charting album by a Kpop Soloist on the chart at the time! "Closer" debuted at #19 on the Billboard Hot R&B Songs chart, with RM becoming the 1st K-Artist to enter the chart! RM became the 1ST Asian Soloist to chart an album and title track at #1 on iTunes in the 8 biggest markets! "Wild Flower" became RM's 1st Hot 100 hit, debuting at #83 and surpassed 100 #1's on ITunes, with 'Indigo' reaching #1 in over 100 countries!  

RM released his 2nd critically acclaimed studio album, 'Right Place, Wrong Person' on May 24, 2024, powered by the hits "Lost" & "Come Back to Me" which reached #24 on the US Hot 100! RM became the 1ST Asian Rapper and the 1ST K-Pop Act of 2024 to debut at #1 on both the Worldwide and European iTunes Song and Album Charts simultaneously! The Album debuted at No. 5 on the Billboard 200 with 54,000 album-equivalent units sold, earning RM his highest debut entry on the chart and the largest opening sales week of his career! The Album also debuted at #1 on the Top Rap Albums chart in America and at No. 2 on the Korean Circle Album Chart with over 585,000 copies sold of its two versions and debuted at No. 2 on the Japanese Oricon Albums Chart with over 23,000 sales. A film documentary, 'RM: Right People, Wrong Place' directed by Lee Seok-jun re the 8-month period before RM's enlistment and the album's creative process, premiered at the Busan International Film Festival in October and was released in theatres globally the following December!  RM has had numerous very successful collabs including "Neva Play" with Megan Thee Stallion which debuted atop the Worldwide, European & US iTunes song charts and broke the record for the highest debut on Pandora by a K-Pop Act with 314,555 streams! In 2020 he was honoured with the Art Patron of the year Award and in 2023 he won Collab & Music Video of the year for his track "Sexy Nukim" at the Korean Hip-hop Awards!  In 2023 he won a SEC award for Asian Musical Artist of the Year and in 2024, he won the MAMA award for 'Fans Choice Top 10 - Male Artist' and the UK Music Video Award for 'Best Alternative Video – International' for "Lost!" Little Simz as one of the best songs of 2024 and RM's 'LOST' was named by Vimeo staff as one of the best short films on the internet! In 2018, RM was awarded the 5th-class Hwagwan Order of Cultural Merit by the President of South Korea for his contributions to spreading Korean culture. On June 1, 2023, RM was appointed the PR Ambassador for South Korea's Ministry of National Defense Agency Remains Excavation and Investigation Team. On June 20, 2026, RM was appointed the first-ever Global Ambassador of the National Museum of Korea!

RM is also a famous Art collector, known for his notable art pieces including Roni Horn's glass sculpture, KAWS figurines and Takeshi Murakami's "Flower Ball (3-D), Kindergarten (2007)". In 2020, RM added to his collection "Disappearing Hometown 730", a luminescent landscape by South Korean artist Joung Young Ju. In June 2025, after his enlistment in the Army, RM was named Global Ambassador for Samsung Art TV, championing the global art scene. RM held a special talk hosted by Samsung Electronics at Art Basel along with Clément Delépine, Director of Art Basel Paris, featuring the artist Basim Magdy! Week 2 CFB Preview 🏈

Texas vs Ohio State (7:30PM) 🔴🔴 

Let's start off with the Longhorns defense. Under Will Muschamp, Texas is going to run more aggressive fronts. You might see the Longhorns line up in five-man fronts or unique blitz packages featuring Rasheem Biles and Justin Cryer. I expect Muschamp to play a lot more man coverage and Cover 3 than Pete Kwiatkowski, who mixed in a ton of hybrid looks, especially Cover 2 and Cover 3. In their previous two matchups against Ohio State, Sarkisian dedicated extra coverage to Jeremiah Smith. I don’t expect that same approach this time because of Texas’s new defensive scheme. Instead, look for Longhorns star cornerback Grayson Littleton to travel with Smith across the field. Ryan Day has also started using Smith all over the formation, including in the slot. The other receiver to watch is Devin McCuin. Last season at UTSA, McCuin averaged 2.43 yards per route run against man coverage. Outside of Littleton and Jelani McDonald, this Longhorns secondary is still very inexperienced, so I expect Arthur Smith to take some deep shots in this matchup.

As for Ohio State’s run game, the Buckeyes’ rushing attack was disappointing in Week 1 against Ball State. They posted just a 45.5% success rate on the ground against a poor rush defense. Now they face a stout Texas defensive line that wants to stop the run under Muschamp. I don’t expect Bo Jackson or Jakobi Jackson to have much success on inside zone. Look for Arthur Smith to lean on Julian Sayin’s arm.

That brings us to Sayin. This Texas front should generate pressure frequently. The right side of Ohio State’s offensive line is not particularly strong in pass protection, and right tackle Phillip Daniels is the weak link. He has a tough assignment against Collin Simmons. Sayin is a completely different quarterback when he is kept clean compared with when he is under pressure.

Julian Sayin when kept clean in 2025:
84.6% adjusted completion rate
127.1 NFL passer rating
93.9 passing grade

Julian Sayin under pressure in 2025:
74.3% adjusted completion rate
96.3 NFL passer rating
68.9 passing grade

If the Buckeyes want to go on the road and pull off an upset, they have to stay in standard downs. I expect Arthur Smith’s game plan to revolve around the quick game if Ohio State cannot run the football. Dropping back 35-plus times against a Muschamp defense is not a recipe for success. I also expect more tempo under Smith. In Week 1, Ohio State averaged 25.6 seconds per play, much faster than last season, when the Buckeyes ranked near the bottom of the country in seconds per play. Whoever wins the line of scrimmage on this side of the ball is going to win the game.

Now to the Longhorns’ offense. Arch Manning is a completely different quarterback than the last time he faced Ohio State. Since the Red River Rivalry game, he has become one of the better quarterbacks in college football. Over that span, he owns a 10-to-4 big-time throw to turnover-worthy play ratio. He has also improved mechanically and looks fully comfortable in Sarkisian’s system.I expect Manning to give this Buckeyes defense trouble. Ohio State’s defense is not the same unit it was last season, especially in the trenches. Without Kayden McDonald, Caden Curry, Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles, and most importantly Caleb Downs, I do not think this group will be the nation’s best defense like it was in 2025. It is still a good unit, but it does not have the same star power. I like Devin Sanchez and Jaylen McClain in the secondary, but they no longer have a roamer like Downs anymore. 

Now let's talk about this matchup. Manning is going to see a lot of man coverage from Matt Patricia, especially Cover 1. Manning has been up and down against that coverage in his career, but I expect Sarkisian to have some answers. With Cam Coleman arriving from the portal and Ryan Wingo getting another year in the system, I expect Texas to take some deep shots at Ohio State’s secondary. Also I expect Arch to have a relatively clean pocket for most of the night because the Buckeyes’ edge rushers outside of Kenyatta Jackson Jr. are unproven. If you give Arch Manning a clean pocket, he's going to score points. Matt Patricia has to find a way to keep Arch in the pocket in this game.  Once Manning gets on the move, he becomes much harder to defend. Look for Patricia’s defense to emphasize some sort of quarterback contain. Overall, Texas should be able to move the ball through the air.

Now let's address the Texas run game. The Longhorns’ rushing attack was disappointing in Week 1. Texas posted just a 37.1% success rate on the ground against a poor Texas State defense. Take away Hollywood Smothers’ 45-yard run, and the starting running backs combined for 20 carries and 59 yards. If Texas wants to make Manning’s job easier, it has to run the ball more efficiently. However even after losing so much NFL talent, Ohio State’s rush defense is still elite, so do not expect Texas to have much success with zone read. Texas is going to be in a ton of knowing passing downs in this game.

Closing Thoughts;

Overall, I do not expect neither team to run the football efficiently. Both offenses should lean on the passing game. This one may come down to whether Texas can score in the red zone. Historically, Sarkisian’s red-zone play calling has hurt the Longhorns in big games. The additions of Cam Coleman and Hollywood Smothers could change that. Manning’s legs are also a real factor near the goal line, and you could see more designed quarterback runs than usual.

I’m picking Texas for two reasons. Manning’s mobility is going to be a huge factor, and Muschamp is going to force Ohio State into being a one-dimensional offense. Once Texas generates pressure on Sayin, he is not the same quarterback. I expect a close game, but I’m trusting the team with more star power playing at home.

I’ve seen a decent amount of media people calling this game a defensive battle. I disagree. Both passing attacks match up pretty well against each other , when both quarterbacks are kept clean. I also do not see either team running the ball efficiently, and I expect both offenses to use more tempo. That combination should lead to points.

This is the most talented roster Sarkisian has ever had. He has to win this football game. Give me the Longhorns.

Michigan vs Oklahoma (12:00PM)

How does Bryce Underwood rebound after that disaster of a performance against Western Michigan? Underwood had five turnover-worthy plays and a 57.1% adjusted completion rate despite being pressured only six times, and that was against a mediocre WMU defense. Now he is facing the best defensive coach in college football in Brent Venables. This Oklahoma defense is dominant in the trenches. You cannot run on this unit, and you cannot sit back and throw on it either. The Sooners dominate every rush concept, especially zone read, which Michigan is going to lean on under Jason Beck. If the Wolverines want to move the football, they are going to need Underwood to bounce back in a major way. Overall, I do not see many avenues for this Michigan offense to have success. Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter are going to be neutralized, and slot receiver JJ Buchanan is going to have a tough day against Oklahoma’s star nickel, Courtland Guillory. The only player on this Michigan offense with a favorable matchup is Andrew Marsh. and even then he has to beat Venables’ heavy Cover 3. Additionally, the Wolverines’ offensive line is not great in pass protection, so I do not see Underwood faring well in passing downs.

If Underwood struggles like he did last week, I would not be shocked to see Kyle Whittingham turn to Tommy Carr early. This Michigan regime is not tied to Underwood in any way.

Now to the other side of the ball. This Oklahoma offense is hard to judge. Sometimes the unit looks like one of the best in college football, and other times it struggles to move the football. In this matchup, I expect the Sooners to have some trouble methodically moving the ball. Oklahoma’s run game under Ben Arbuckle has been inconsistent. Last season the Sooners ranked 107th in rushing success rate, and this unit is not much improved in 2026. The running back room is not anything special, and the offensive line still has questions. Left tackle Michael Fasusi is also expected to be out. Because of that, I expect Michigan to load the box and force John Mateer to beat them as a passer.The strength of Michigan’s defense is the secondary, led by the cornerback duo of Jyaire Hill and Smith Snowden and safety Rod Moore. If Oklahoma cannot run the football efficiently, the Sooners are going to be forced into obvious passing downs. That said, this offense does have the weapons to create explosives. Both Isaiah Sategna and Trell Harris are over 2.0 yards per route run, so I could see Mateer hitting one of them against Jyaire Hill’s Cover 1 looks. For the most part, though, I expect Oklahoma to rely on the quick game and Mateer’s legs. The key for Michigan is dominating the line of scrimmage on this side of the ball. Dom Nichols and Cam Brandt are the guys to watch.

Overall, it is hard to go against Oklahoma here. Underwood mechanically does not look right as a passer, and he is facing one of the better defenses in the country. Still, I would not go running to the window to bet Oklahoma -4.5 on the road in the Big House.

I expect this to be a lower-scoring game, and I do not see either offense doing much. If Michigan wants any shot at an upset, the Wolverines have to establish some kind of run game, whether that is with Underwood’s legs or Marshall and Hiter breaking off an explosive run or two.

Until Underwood improves as a passer or Whittingham goes to Tommy Carr, it is hard to trust this Michigan offense.

Oklahoma 20
Michigan 16

Lean: Oklahoma team total under, if I were to play anything in this game.

Arizona State vs Texas A&M (12:00PM)

Texas A&M’s offense should have no problem running zone read with Rueben Owens and Marcel Reed in this game. In Week 1, the Sun Devils owned just a 43.5% success rate against the rush and an 8.7% stuff rate against an FCS opponent. This unit projects as middle of the pack against the run this season, so we will have to wait and see. As for A&M’s passing attack, Mario Craver and Ashton Bethel-Roman match up pretty well against an unproven Arizona State secondary. I’m intrigued to see what Brian Ward draws up defensively to limit the Aggies’ rushing and passing attack.

On the other side, Cutter Boley is going to have a tough task against this Aggies secondary. It is a good-on-good matchup between Arizona State’s receivers and Texas A&M’s defensive backs. Omarion Miller looks like a future first-round pick, and Reed Harris looks like another legitimate weapon. That said, this Aggies secondary is very good, led by safeties Marcus Ratcliffe and Dalton Brooks. I expect most of Boley’s throws to be short and intermediate. If Arizona State wants to keep this game close, the Sun Devils have to establish some kind of ground game with Kyson Brown. The weakness of this A&M defense is its rush defense, specifically against inside zone, so I expect a heavy dosage of Kyson early. If Arizona State falls behind early, it is going to be tough to come back. Boley is not really the quarterback who will beat you with his arm. He is the type who methodically beats you.

Overall, I do see A&M winning this game, but I do not know if the Aggies cover. I have a ton of respect for Kenny Dillingham and this Arizona State staff, and without Colin Klein calling plays anymore, I do think this Aggies offense takes a slight step back this year. The key for Arizona State covering will be staying in standard downs and avoiding a big early deficit.

Lean: Cutter Boley passing props or some sort of Rueben Owens attempts prop.

Oklahoma State vs Oregon (12:00PM)

I want to back Oregon in this game after how bad Oklahoma State looked offensively, but this Ducks defense still has some serious issues that need to be addressed. That is especially true at the corner spot opposite Brandon Finney, and the defensive line was not as dominant as I anticipated.On the other side, Oregon should have no problem moving the football up and down the field. Oklahoma State’s defense is bad, and Dante Moore is going to have all day to throw in the pocket.

The spread should be Oregon -21, but after how poorly Oklahoma State looked in Week 1, this number is slightly inflated. I would pass at the current price. It is more of a live spot with the Ducks than a pregame bet.

Alabama vs Kentucky (3:30PM)

Lean - Over and Kenny Minchey Passing Props

I’m intrigued to see how Kenny Minchey fares against one of the better secondaries in college football. Stein’s offense matches up pretty well against Kane Wommack’s defense. On the other side, Alabama should still be able to move the football fairly efficiently. Kalen DeBoer has struggled in these kinds of spots over the past two years at Alabama, so it would not shock me if Kentucky won.

Arizona vs BYU (3:30PM)

The Arizona Wildcats lost eight defensive backs after the 2025 season, four to the NFL Draft and four to graduation, so Brett Brennan had a tough task replacing that group this offseason. What made Arizona’s defense so good last year was the secondary, led by Traydun Stukes and Genesis Smith. In this matchup, though, that loss may not matter as much. BYU wants to line up in heavier personnel and run zone read with LJ Martin and Bear Bachmeier.The good news for the Wildcats is they return six key starters in the front seven, including Tre Smith and Mays Pese, so Arizona could have some success slowing down that zone-read attack. At the same time, BYU’s offensive line is good and experienced. That makes the chess match between Danny Gonzales and Aaron Roderick one of the more interesting parts of this game. Which team is going to establish the line of scrimmage?If Arizona can stop the BYU rushing attack, this Cougars offense is limited in passing downs. Outside of freshman wide receiver Legend Glasker and Jojo Phillips, BYU’s receiver room lacks explosiveness on the outside. I expect a heavy dosage of LJ Martin. I know it was last season, but the Wildcats owned just an 18.4% stuff rate and they return a decent amount of that starting front seven. Do not be shocked if Martin has a massive game.

On the other side, even with Jay Hill gone, you are still going to see a ton of Cover 1 and Cover 3 from new defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga. This BYU defense should still be good against the pass and the run, but I do have some concerns with safety Raider Damuni out. Without Damuni, I expect the Cougars to lean a little more on Cover 3, which is a coverage Noah Fifita can take advantage of. Arizona’s receiver room is deep, and when Fifita has time in the pocket, he can dissect a defense. The Wildcats should also get Ismail Mahdi back, which is a huge boost to the rushing attack.The key to Arizona keeping this game close will be Fifita playing a clean game and getting the ball out quickly and on time. Overall, the Wildcats should be able to move the football, but I have some concerns once they get near the red zone.

Lean: Arizona at 8 or higher. My power ratings have this at BYU -9, so I am not going to touch the game. I am going to sit back and collect some data on both teams.Huge game for Big 12 implications.

UCF vs Pittsburgh (3:30PM)

Mason Heintschel has taken a massive leap from his freshman season. In Week 1, he posted a 90.6 PFF passing grade with five big-time throws against a respectable Chuck Harris defense. Now the Panthers face a UCF secondary that could be tested in this matchup.On the other side, Pitt has fielded elite rush defenses year after year under Pat Narduzzi. That matters here because Scott Frost’s scheme is heavily reliant on a ground-based attack. I do not expect the Knights to have any real success running the football. Look for UCF’s offense to rely on Alonza Barnett’s arm.

Lean: Pitt if it gets down to 7 or lower. The Panthers’ offense should be able to move the football up and down the field, but I would avoid betting a side.

I also do not mind some Dylan Wade receiving props. Narduzzi likes to run a ton of quarters, which is a favorable coverage for tight ends. Last season against zone, Wade owned a 22.8% target share and averaged 1.97 yards per route run. He should be Alonza Barnett’s safety blanket in this game.

Cal vs Syracuse (3:30PM)

No lean in this game for me. Syracuse has the corners to match up with Cal’s wide receivers, and this Cal defense got destroyed on the ground last week. The Golden Bears posted just a 3.5% stuff rate against UCLA. It is hard for me to back a team that is weak in the trenches on both sides of the football.

On the Syracuse side, Steve Angeli looked great in his first game back from injury, and wide receiver Umari Hatcher has emerged in this offense. If Tosh Lupoi did not run so much two-high shell coverage, I would look at Hatcher props. Other than that, I am passing on this game completely.

My numbers like Cal, but I do not trust JKS on the road, and this Cal offensive line fails to get a push in the run game. The Golden Bears owned just a 30.8% rushing success rate last week.

Ms State vs Minnesota (3:30PM)

Kamario Taylor is quickly turning into one of the better quarterbacks in college football, but this is not the spot to fade the Gophers. Under P.J. Fleck, Minnesota has consistently fielded good secondaries, and I do not see many avenues for explosives for this Bulldogs offense.

On the other side, Minnesota should be able to control the trenches with its inside-zone rushing attack led by Darius Taylor. The weakness of the Mississippi State defense is the front seven, while the strength is the secondary led by stud corner Kelly Jones. As long as Drake Lindsey plays a clean football game, the Gophers should be able to win with the run game. Arnett’s aggressive defense should also play into Minnesota’s favor.

Lean: Minnesota, but I do not see much of an edge to bet on it.

UTSA vs Texas State (3:30PM)

Under Jeff Traylor, the Roadrunners have always had drastic home-and-away splits. Now they face one of the most explosive offenses in the entire G6 in Texas State on the road. The Bobcats might have lost by 52 last week to Texas, but they still generated 349 yards of offense, and I do not see this UTSA defense stopping the passing attack led by Brad Jackson and Beau Sparks. Last season, the Roadrunners ranked 131st in pass explosives allowed. It is also going to be near 100 degrees at kickoff in San Marcos, which is not ideal for stopping a fast-tempo offense like Texas State’s.

This should be a fun back-and-forth game, but I like the Bobcats to score some points at home. My numbers have this closer to Texas State -3.

Lean - Texas State TT O

Tennessee vs Georgia Tech (7:00PM)

Georgia Tech was stuffed on 44.4% of its rushes last week. Something has to change this week for Brent Key’s offense. I expect Alberto Mendoza to throw the ball more and for his legs to be used more in the zone-read game. The strength of this Tennessee defense under Jim Knowles should be the front, so I do not expect George Godsey to constantly spam inside zone with Justice Haynes. The key to Georgia Tech moving the football will be finding Jordan Allen on the outside. Allen averaged 4.52 yards per route run against Colorado last week and projects as a guy around 2.5 YPRR for the season. He has to have a big day if Georgia Tech wants to pull off the upset.

On the Tennessee side, the Volunteers’ offense under Josh Heupel is always going to be excellent. The Yellow Jackets do not have the personnel to defend the Veer and Shoot, so I do not see many avenues for success on that side of the ball. Running back DeSean Bishop should have no problem running inside zone, and receivers Mike Matthews and Braylon Staley should be mismatch targets on the outside. That said, this will be Brandon Faizon’s first true test, and he is still only 18 years old, so I could see him struggling. Overall, I still expect Tennessee’s offense to methodically move the football.

Brent Key is 17-6 ATS in his career as an underdog, and I make this game Tennessee -10. The Volunteers could win by two touchdowns, but the right pregame side is Georgia Tech.

I am likely not going to bet on this game. 

I also hate fading Heupel in out-of-conference games, because he has been a covering machine.

Iowa State vs Iowa (7:30PM)

Cy-Hawk games are usually fun, lower-scoring defensive matchups, but this Iowa State team is not the same as last season. Matt Campbell left for Penn State, and in comes Jimmy Rogers from Washington State, who is at best a mediocre coach. The Hawkeyes should have no problem running the football against an Iowa State defense that projects as below average against the run. Kamari Moulton averaged a ridiculous 9.36 yards after first contact last week. Also In Week 1, the Cyclones owned just a 14.6% stuff rate, which is well below national average.

On the other side, Jaylon Raynor is going to have issues against Phil Parker’s Cover 4-heavy defense. Iowa State’s wide receiver room is not great, and I do not see the Cyclones running the football efficiently in this game. Iowa should be able to run the ball comfortably and win by two-plus possessions.

I like Kamari Moulton props, but I would avoid a side in this rivalry game because both teams operate at a very slow tempo. You also want to back Phil Parker as a dog, not as a large favorite.

Arkansas vs Utah (10:15PM)

Arkansas was stuffed on 21.7% of its rushes against North Alabama, of all opponents. So far, Ryan Silverfield’s tenure at Arkansas is off to a slow start, and I do not see it getting much better going into Rice-Eccles Stadium at night. Utah should be able to establish the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, and I do not see this Razorbacks defense having much success stopping the zone-read attack from Dampier and Wayshawn Parker. Even if Arkansas loads the box to take away the Utes’ rushing attack, Dampier should be able to pick apart this zone-heavy Ron Roberts defense.

On the other side, I am super low on this Razorbacks offense this season. The offensive line is not great, and KJ Jackson struggles as an intermediate passer. Morgan Scalley’s aggressive 4-2-5 defense is going to give Jackson some trouble in this game.

My numbers make this game Utah -10.1, so I show no value on the spread. Instead, I would look at some Sutton Smith receiving props, because KJ Jackson is going to check the football down a ton in this game.
